chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to perform the Ziyarah of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), perform it while you are in grief, distressed, dishevelled, dusty, hungry, and thirsty, and ask him for your needs, and leave from him, and do not take it as a homeland.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended spiritual state and etiquette when performing Ziyarah to Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* prescribes a state of profound humility and existential need (*faqir*) when visiting Imam Al-Husayn, using physical signs of distress like being dusty and hungry to reflect inner spiritual poverty. It instructs the visitor to treat the shrine as a place of supplication rather than a permanent residence (*watan*), emphasizing the transient nature of the visit and the enduring connection to the Imam. This practice aligns with the Shia tradition of *Ziyarat* as a means of drawing closer to divine grace through the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from one our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you intend to perform the Ziyarah of Al-Husaynasws, so perform it while you are in grief, distressed, dishevelled, dusty, hungry, thirsty, and ask himasws for the needs, and leave from himasws and do not take it as a homeland’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from certain individuals of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that if you wish to visit al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, you should visit him when you feel sad, faced with hardship, in an untidy physical condition, hungry and thirsty. Ask him to help you for your wishes, then move away and do not adopt it as your place of residence.”
